clue.text: Could be a Mexican fancy chair ornament (5,8)

indicators.note: fancy as a verb-like adjective: the letters are made elaborate, rearranged

explanation.surface: A carved decoration on a chair, perhaps in a Mexican furniture style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' flags a definition by example: a Mexican is one kind of North American. 'Fancy' reads as describing the chair, but it tells you to rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is in North America, so a Mexican is an example of a North American.

clue.text: Government error (9)

blocks.note: supervision or control, as a watchdog exercises over an agency
a slip, something missed by not looking

explanation.surface: A complaint about a blunder by the people in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two nearly opposite senses: watching over something, and failing to notice it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversight means both supervision and an inadvertent mistake.

clue.text: Tense little bird hiding garish wings (5)

indicators.note: the bird holds the other letters inside it
a word's wings are its two outer letters

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small, nervous bird concealing its gaudy plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' sounds like part of the bird, but it takes the ends of 'garish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight muscles or a tight situation are tense ones.

clue.text: Laura goes mad, according to hearsay (5)

indicators.note: the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Gossip claims that a woman called Laura has lost her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to hearsay' looks like a homophone signal, but it is the definition: aural means received by the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Aural means relating to hearing, so what is aural comes by way of the ear, as hearsay does.

clue.text: Candidates name exes I harassed (9)

indicators.note: the letters are harried into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confessing that the candidates are former partners they once pestered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candidates' suggests election hopefuls, and the surface pulls toward romance; the fodder is simply 'name exes I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: those sitting a test are its candidates.

clue.text: Almost all at sea? (2,3,4)

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A question: is nearly everything adrift?
explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' is an idiom for confused, which hides the split: 'Almost all' is one definition and 'at sea' the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main means mostly; literally it also means out on the ocean.

clue.text: Corridor is drenched in beer (5)

indicators.note: IS is soaked in, so surrounded by, the beer

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A hallway flooded with spilt beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drenched in' paints a spill; as wordplay it only means surrounded by.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, a corridor.

clue.text: Probability governs this torture for a wage slave (3,2,8)

indicators.note: the letters are twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: A complaint that grinding work is torment for the poorly paid employee.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase rather than a synonym: the law of averages is the principle probability is said to obey.
explanation.definitionFit: The law of averages is the popular name for the idea that chance evens out over many trials.

clue.text: Freedom fighter lends a lone man ingredients (6,7)

indicators.note: the letters are ingredients to be mixed into something new

explanation.surface: A resistance fighter supplies provisions to a solitary man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lone man' suits the answer, who spent 27 years in prison before leading South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Mandela fought apartheid and became South Africa's first Black president.

clue.text: Someone getting even with a vice principal before green revolution (7)

indicators.note: the principal, or chief, letter of vice is its first
the letters of green are turned about
V comes ahead of the rearranged green

explanation.surface: Someone settling a score with the school's deputy head before an environmental uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice principal' reads as a deputy head teacher; split it and 'principal' asks for the first letter of 'vice'.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenger is someone who takes revenge, getting even.

clue.text: Upstart is temporarily hiding performer (7)

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters span the end of 'upstart', all of 'is' and the start of 'temporarily'

explanation.surface: A cocky newcomer is lying low for a while, concealing an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstart' reads as a noun, a brash newcomer; the answer straddles three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym with a theatrical flavour: the French-derived word for a stage entertainer.

clue.text: Start working with clique (5)

blocks.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: Advice to begin a job alongside a tight group of friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start working' reads as one instruction, but 'Start' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for beginning, as of an illness or a season.

clue.text: They hang around it or reel around on Sunday (9)

indicators.note: the letters are turned around into a new order
S is placed after the rearranged letters

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: People loafing near something or staggering about on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'around' belongs to the definition; the second rearranges IT OR REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Loiterers are people who hang around with no purpose.

clue.text: Protection for first of ministers to be airbrushed from explosive images (5)

indicators.note: take the initial letter of ministers
airbrushing removes something from a picture, so M is removed
the remaining letters are blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Politicians airbrushed out of damaging photographs to shield them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airbrushed from' fits photos perfectly, which disguises a plain deletion: IMAGES loses M, then IAGES is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the aegis of someone means under their protection; the aegis was Zeus's shield.

clue.text: Separate people struggle for universal supremacy (5,4)

explanation.surface: Divided groups fighting for dominance over everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Universal' is the wit: the contest was literally about the universe. The space race was the Cold War rivalry between the USA and USSR to reach space and the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the Cold War contest was literally over the cosmos, so 'universal' is exact.

clue.text: Undertaking talk about school sport (9)

indicators.note: the talk goes around the school sport

blocks.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A lecture on sport in schools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk about' reads as one phrase meaning discuss; split, 'about' wraps the talk around the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is an undertaking, an organised piece of work.

clue.text: Musicians put together alternative cabinet in conjunction with artist (9)

blocks.note: a chest is a piece of storage furniture

explanation.surface: Players assemble a rival government alongside an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative cabinet' reads as a shadow government; here cabinet is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of musicians brought together to play.

clue.text: False mitigation strangely lacking in gravity (9)

indicators.note: the letters come out in a strange order
G is missing from the word

blocks.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A dishonest plea in mitigation, oddly lacking seriousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' sounds like seriousness, fitting a courtroom plea, but it only supplies G.
explanation.definitionFit: Imitation leather is false leather; as a modifier, imitation means fake.

clue.text: Grips mouths (9)

blocks.note: holds spellbound, stress on the second syllable
ways in, as the mouth of a cave; stress on the first syllable

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently, stress on the second syllable for enchanting and on the first for doorways.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip an audience is to entrance it; a cave's mouth is its entrance.

clue.text: Gun lobbyists accept first rate funds in Nigeria (5)

indicators.note: the lobbyists take AI inside them

blocks.note: the NRA is the US National Rifle Association
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as I

explanation.surface: Gun lobbyists take a bribe of top-notch cash in Nigeria.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a classic grade for the best, and crosswords routinely write it AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: the name of the Nigerian currency.

clue.text: Understanding an address about workers (9)

indicators.note: the address goes around the workers

blocks.note: to greet is to address someone
men = workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Grasping the point of a speech about the labour force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a noun, a speech; here it is the verb, to greet.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: two sides reaching an understanding have come to terms.

clue.text: Components of immigration quota (5)

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters that are parts of the next word

blocks.note: the five letters sit inside the word, after IMMIG

explanation.surface: The parts that make up an immigration limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Components of' says the answer is made from parts of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a quota fixes a share, a proportion of the whole.

clue.text: Opener for Kent is dismissed from dodgy wicket more than once (5)

indicators.note: the opening letter of Kent
K is sent away from the word
the remaining letters are unreliable, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Kent's opening batsman is out on a bad pitch, and not for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is all misdirection: Kent is an English county side, an opener is a first batsman, a wicket is the pitch. Here the opener is just K.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: two times is the least that counts as more than once.

clue.text: Reportedly remained sober (5)

indicators.note: as it is reported, spoken aloud

blocks.note: a past tense meaning remained, said aloud

explanation.surface: Word is that someone stayed on the wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober' here means serious and sedate, not off the drink as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of sedate and serious.

clue.text: More diffident heirs relaxed (5)

indicators.note: the letters are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: Timid heirs start to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relaxed' is the opposite of shy, which helps hide it as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of shy, in the standard variant spelling with an I.

clue.text: Antique pamphlet clipping (7)

blocks.note: a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: An old leaflet cut from a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipping' looks like part of the surface, a verb or a press cutting; as the definition it means an excerpt.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a passage cut from a larger text.

clue.text: Opening in it, I joined up with a novice (7)

blocks.note: L = learner, from the L-plates on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: Someone describing their first step: they signed up alongside a beginner.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word but 'novice' is taken at face value; only the L needs decoding.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym: the opening stage is the first one.

clue.text: Solids hardened, so doc set to work (13)

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, rearranged

explanation.surface: Some materials have set hard, so the doctor gets on with the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solids' reads as the material that hardened, but it means geometric solids; 'so' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodecahedron is a solid with twelve faces.
